title: Does instruction-tuning on shared data erase diversity? A before/after homogeneity comparison

original_idea.body:
# Does instruction-tuning erase diversity?

Pair open base models with their instruct counterparts; on fixed prompts measure inter-model homogeneity within base vs instruct sets to test homogenization-by-alignment. Public checkpoints on a consumer GPU; no training.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 3: plausible root-cause chain (alignment as homogenizer) but link to catastrophic risk is diffuse.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: pair base/instruct, measure inter-model similarity on fixed prompts; standard tooling.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped base-vs-instruct homogeneity comparison with clear criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: public base+instruct checkpoints, root-cause work, no internal access, weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on base+instruct pairs + embeddings, single GPU; base models can be larger.

novelty.reasoning: Instruction-tuning effects discussed; the explicit base-vs-instruct homogeneity test may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Homogenization-by-alignment hypothesis is plausibly underexplored as a direct before/after test.
